preservation_map.claim: # Authentication and sessions
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Overview
This candidate topic consolidates portal user authentication, session design, and Entra migration materials. It separates user-stated intent from source proposals and historical evidence, and it does not establish deployed behavior, approved security policy, or approval authority. Its main contribution is a structured map of authentication and session responsibilities, plus the gaps that block policy publication. The target portal authenticates users, obtains entitlements, and issues tokens for application requests.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Portal entry and entitlements
- User-stated intent: an authenticated SC user with no entitlement for any registered application entity must be denied portal entry in local, test, UAT, and production. The [[entities/portal-team]] is named as owner only by user report; authority and approval are unconfirmed. The answer defines no HTTP status, denial wording, or entity-versus-role semantics.
- Draft principles state the same denial direction. An older tile-security proposal instead permits SC entry; it remains conflicting historical evidence, not selected intent.
- Separate user-stated rules: deny tiles without a configured [[entities/ems2]] entity; allow tile visibility and launch through the empty-subject rule when one EMS2 entity is configured and zero subjects are configured, owned by the [[entities/portal-team]] across the same environments.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Links: [[concepts/portal-entry-and-tile-authorization]], [[concepts/ems2-entitlement-provisioning]], [[summaries/KT-sdk-and-entitlements]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Intended session renewal
The RATAN team owns and reviews portal policy under ICS bank security policy. The user set ceilings of 15 minutes idle and 60 minutes absolute from portal authentication. Eligible mouse, keyboard, and scroll activity supports renewal within the absolute deadline, including across initial refresh credential expiry while access remains valid. At the deadline, further access requires a new authenticated portal session. Before the deadline, the prior idle-prompt recovery keeps the prompt open while renewal is pending, closes it once after success, and permits another eligible attempt after rejection.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The ideal logout target immediately revokes all of the user's portal sessions. Protected actions and renewals using those sessions should fail after logout completes. Entra and other identity-provider sessions are outside that revocation scope. The [logout criterion](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-authentication-and-sessions.md#portal-logout-ac-001) remains a candidate for RATAN review.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Links: [[concepts/session-activity-renewal]], [[concepts/session-expiry-prompt-recovery]], [[summaries/REQ-active-session-renewal]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Authentication responsibilities and Entra migration
- Entra design: browser redirect, authorization-code exchange through the [[entities/single-ui-bff]]; the BFF builds user information, retrieves [[entities/ems2]] entitlements, and issues authentication and entitlement tokens. The historical design retained OneMFA fallback and described a separate username/password path. The current production target prohibits OneMFA fallback. [Sign-in criterion](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-authentication-and-sessions.md#portal-sso-ac-001).
- Phase 1 covers UI SSO only. It excludes EMS2 replacement, portal session management, and tenant-onboarding authentication. Machine-to-machine authentication has a separate migration document with unresolved central dependencies.
- Non-production verification requires a development AD account, Authenticator registration, and RATAN AD-group membership; it checks successful login, user information, and expected tile visibility. The FAQ ties missing entitlements to tile access and EMS2 configuration.
- The production pilot describes Windows Hello or Authenticator login and a one-hour [[entities/entra]] session; that provider session does not settle the portal refresh-token lifetime. It also warns that AD profile values differ from OUD values: surname formatting, country codes, and missing locale values can affect downstream audit or application logic.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Links: [[concepts/identity-provider-delegation]], [[entities/entra]], [[concepts/identity-profile-attribute-migration]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Session concepts and historical timing proposals
The source distinguishes an access token for application requests, an idle timeout for inactivity, an absolute timeout since authentication, and a refresh token for another authentication interval without repeating the initial SSO journey. These are documented concepts, not a confirmed runtime contract.
- Session version 0 states limits below 60 minutes for absolute timeout and below 15 minutes for idle timeout. Its examples use a 15-minute access token and a 24-hour refresh token. It proposes an inactivity warning, session extension, single-device login, and reused-token rejection.
- Session version 1 proposes `exp = iat + 15 minutes` for idle timeout, ties absolute timeout to `auth_time` and a 60-minute `max_age`, obtains a refresh token before access-token expiry, and exchanges it at a later relogin. Single-device login and token blacklist work sit on a backlog.
- Version 1 conflicts with itself: it contains both 105-minute and 225-minute refresh-token durations, proposes changing `auth_time` during continued activity, and also says refresh tokens have no absolute timeout because they lack `auth_time` and `max_age`. These competing durations are historical proposals. The latest clarification sets the two session ceilings and leaves individual token lifetimes open.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Links: [[concepts/token-lifecycle-and-timeout-policy]], [[concepts/session-activity-renewal]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Historical machine-to-machine authentication
The historical [[entities/fmaa]] reference describes client-credential authentication for machine-to-machine callers, separates service-account onboarding from bank-ID onboarding, and describes OUD-managed accounts authenticated through FMAA. It states 17-year validity for service accounts and seven-day validity for bank IDs. These historical values do not establish approved portal-session limits or current token policy.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Links: [[concepts/machine-to-machine-authentication]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Evidence limits and open questions
The 12 November answer assigns policy ownership to RATAN. The applicable ICS revision and environment-specific timeout and token values require review. Open questions include authorization to initiate logout when the access token has already expired, the intended profile contract, and the applicability of historical FMAA flows. Retained sources supply no deployed enforcement or publication decision.

preservation_map.claim: # CES Migration Permission Preservation
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Overview
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: This topic defines the intended preservation of permission meaning when migrating from EMS2 production to CES UAT, covering mapped entitlement definitions and permission content for all scoped accounts. It also sets frontend compatibility and independent per-tile migration intent for `mfe-base`, the shared Ratan container, and their upper applications.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Scope is controlled by a series of user clarifications dated 3–9 November 2026. The document is a `candidate` draft and records user-stated intent, not verified execution.

preservation_map.claim: ## EMS2-to-CES concept mapping
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
| EMS2 concept | CES concept | Comparison boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Role | Entitlement | Compare mapped definition and assigned accounts |
| Entity | Application | Preserve application scope when comparing names |
| Subject | Feature | Compare through explicit feature mapping |
| Action | Action | Compare permitted operation within mapped feature |
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Names shared across different applications do not establish equivalent permissions, and numeric source identifiers may differ without changing mapped meaning. See [[concepts/ems2-to-ces-permission-mapping]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Preservation requirements
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ### Entitlement and account parity
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The intended migration has no missing mapped entitlements or permission gaps, but that is an expectation, not retained proof. Entitlement definitions must be compared before catalog totals are treated as completeness evidence. Different entitlements can yield the same combined effective permissions without proving equal definitions or assignments. See [[summaries/KT-sdk-and-entitlements]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Account comparisons must include every account in the selected entity scope, expand multi-ID cells, and count each distinct account once. Application and entitlement scope must be retained, and data restrictions must be compared through authoritative definitions and resolved values—not profile names alone.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ### Coverage and FMO exception
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Fully matched migrated content moves into coverage totals and out of the active difference list; missing, additional, unresolved, and unavailable comparisons stay visible. An unavailable comparison proves neither equality nor missing permissions.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: FMO Portal Admin is excluded from the production comparison and tracked as a separate, lower-priority non-production item. Its content must not enter production coverage denominators.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Frontend compatibility and per-tile migration
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The primary objective is compatibility with existing upper-application APIs, adapting provider-specific identities and permission data internally. Non-unique roles are the known compatibility gap; this does not prove every other API is compatible.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ### Independent tile provider selection
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Each tile selects its entitlement provider independently. An EMS2 tile keeps existing admission logic; a CES tile uses CES admission logic, configured application identity, and CES permission structure. Moving one tile to CES must not force changes on unrelated tiles. In the migration contract, `EMS2 (CES)` denotes the CES path with wire value `EMS3`. See [[concepts/per-tile-provider-selection]] and [[concepts/portal-entry-and-tile-authorization]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ### Provider-union hasPermission
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Existing `hasPermission(code)` calls may accept a mapped grant from either EMS2 or CES. The check must log which provider supplied an accepted grant and must not require a new caller scope argument. This shared functional check is separate from tile admission. See [[concepts/permission-check-provider-union]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ### Role multiplicity and CES role-owned writes
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Multiple assigned CES roles must not be collapsed into one proven role, and callers expecting a scalar role require a sourced business mapping. CES saved-view and filter writes that require one owner role stay disabled until an ownership rule is agreed; no primary role may be selected and no comma-joined role names may be submitted as a scalar owner. Existing EMS2 role-owned writes keep their behavior. See [[concepts/ces-role-multiplicity]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## CES entity fields
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Two new fields are required on EMS3 entities: `roleList` and `applicationId`. The table also records clarified values for the existing `name` and `applicationName` fields; those two existing fields are retained rather than introduced as additional new fields.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
| Field | Required value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roleList` | CES `entitlements.entitlement_name` values | Application-scoped assignment names |
| `applicationId` | CES application `itam_id` (e.g. `"51358"`) | CES application identity |
| `name` | `RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_RULE` | CES application/entity name for EMS2 `X_RATANONE` |
| `applicationName` | `RATAN` | Legacy team/display label |
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: CES `user_data.app_name` supplies the CES authorization name, not the legacy team label. These additions must not remove existing fields or change EMS2 decisions, and they do not resolve scalar role semantics. See [[entities/ratan]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Acceptance criteria
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
- **FE-ROLE-WRITE-AC-001** — Zero CES role-owned write requests or fabricated scalar owners before an ownership rule exists; zero rule-induced EMS2 decision changes.
- **FE-COMPAT-AC-001** — Zero contradictory decisions for mapped feature/action permissions through existing caller APIs.
- **FE-COMPAT-AC-002** — Each tile admits through its selected provider with zero unrelated-application admissions.
- **FE-COMPAT-AC-003** — One tile may switch provider with zero forced changes on other tiles and zero required call-signature changes.
- **FE-COMPAT-AC-004** — `hasPermission(code)` returns the union of EMS2 and CES grants across four cases, with no extra arguments and provider-source logs for accepted decisions.
- **BFF-ENTITY-AC-001** — `roleList` contains the application's entitlement names with zero names imported from another application.
- **BFF-ENTITY-AC-002** — `applicationId`, `name`, and `applicationName` match declared values with zero legacy substitutions.
- **BFF-ENTITY-AC-003** — Additive metadata changes zero EMS2 decisions and removes zero existing fields.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Overview
This topic links release planning with [[concepts/configuration-promotion]] and [[concepts/tenant-production-readiness]]. The supplied materials mix procedures, an unfinished checklist, historical deployment guidance, and a release proposal whose current authority is unconfirmed.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Responsibilities
The release proposal assigns Portal routing, route enabling, tenant interfaces, and Portal-owned production changes to Portal teams. Tenant teams retain responsibility for their UI, backend, services, databases, and infrastructure. Portal teams run Portal releases and routing rollback; tenant teams validate applications, perform UVT, and support tenant issues.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Readiness and scheduling
Requested inputs include solution intent, user profiles, routing details, connectivity checks, UAT sign-off, and rollback planning; new interfaces require 30 days of engagement under the proposal. The unfinished checklist adds SDK validation, shared frontend requests, entitlement checks, disaster recovery, performance inputs, operating agreements, and penetration testing. The unfinished checklist also calls for tenant review with RATAN before preparing each production release and assigns the tenant the upstream disaster-recovery check. The portal load balancer has no DR responsibility in that checklist. This guidance requires applicability review. [Canonical readiness section](../../../records/candidates/operations/KT-release-operations.md#readiness-before-scheduling).
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Configuration promotion
The documented flow starts with Module Map, Drawer Category, and Tile Configuration changes in Development. Teams export CSV files to a tenant-owned repository, then an ADO pipeline uploads configuration to the Portal Admin service at `/api/auth/v1/fmo/admin/config/upload`. The flow says the service validates an FMAA JWT before processing CSV files. The first bulk insert into UAT and Production uses a separate BFF release; later uploads depend on tenant connectivity. The checklist also flags planned FMAA decommissioning, creating an unresolved dependency.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Tenant capabilities in requests
Release requests describe intended business functions: FSS Cash Projection, FSS Funds Gating, FSS SSI, FSS Domestic Disbursement, FSS Gold Custody, FSS Digital Asset Collateral, DDR Reporting, CDUPS Confirmation, VPA Fix Link, and VPA Trade Monitor. These show why tenant tiles need Portal integration; they do not establish approved rules, completion, or present availability.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Release window proposal
[[concepts/release-window-governance]] is proposed rather than confirmed. The proposal schedules first, third, and available fifth Saturdays at 09:00 SGT, freezes scope after Monday EOD in the first week, cancels windows without requests, and requires approved exceptions for late additions. Freeze periods need rescheduling or dispensation. Two ambiguities remain: the summary says 24 hours while the table says 10 hours ending at 19:00 SGT; the urgent-release section requires all confirmations but also permits proceeding when nobody raises concerns. Silence and explicit confirmation are different conditions.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:

Tenant onboarding requires separate evidence for technical deployment and business activation. The release calendar separates Portal release dates from tenant release dates and lists separate Entra technical and business go-live entries. preservation_map.claim: # SDK and Entitlements
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Overview
This topic connects [[concepts/single-ui-sdk-authentication]] with [[concepts/entitlement-retrieval]] and the boundary between portal tile access and application data permissions. It separates documented SDK behavior from user-stated policy intent and from unverified deployment or approval evidence.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Key concepts
- [[concepts/single-ui-sdk-authentication]]: The [[entities/single-ui-sdk]] injects an HTTP request filter that validates Single UI JWTs and exposes user context through the `userInfo` request attribute.
- [[concepts/entitlement-retrieval]]: Services can query [[entities/ems2]] through `AuthorizationService.getEntitlements` or extract a separate entitlement token through `JwtTokenUtil.getEntitlementsToken`. An entitlement token must not be used for authentication or login.
- Portal entry policy: An authenticated SC user with no entitlement for any registered application entity must be denied portal entry in local, test, UAT, and production. This is user-stated intent only.
- Tile security and empty configuration: Empty EMS2 entity configuration hides the tile and denies direct launch; empty subject configuration allows visibility and launch through the tile's one configured entity. Portal access remains separate from application data permissions.
- CES entitlement migration: EMS2 `X_RATANONE` was renamed to CES `RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_RULE`. The clarification confirms a name correspondence only, not identifier or role equivalence.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Documented SDK behavior and versions
- Version 1.0.0 documents artifact `com.scb.ratan:single-ui-sdk-starter`, configuration prefix `single-ui-sdk.auth`, optional `user-login-max-duration`, and request context field `userEntitlements`.
- Version 1.1.1 renames the artifact to `com.scb.fmoportal:fmoportal-auth-sdk`, removes the duration property, and renames the field to `entitlements`.
- Version 1.1.2 adds `max_age` validation and `oud` in request context.
- Version 1.1.4 documents logout session rejection and configurable public certificates. Its Java guides expose `userId`, `entitlements`, `oud`, and `sessionId` through `userInfo`.
- Declared variants include Java 8 `1.1.4-java8` with Spring Boot 2.6.6 or higher, Java 17 `1.1.4-java17` with Spring Boot 3.1.2 or higher, and a Boot 4 migration note for `2.0.0-SNAPSHOT` on Spring Boot 4.0.6. An official `2.0.0` release remains conditional on regression testing.
- The URL algorithm checks exclusions first. With an empty inclusion list, all remaining paths are validated; otherwise only matching inclusion paths are validated. `skip-jwt-headers` can bypass JWT checks, but the documents do not identify a trusted replacement control.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## SDK 3.0.0 CES migration intent
The user selected SDK version `3.0.0`. The migration must preserve the old contract where possible and assess complete compatibility. The SDK caller supplies the FMAA token, and tests are required. Failure handling remains unresolved and open to engineering suggestions.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
Acceptance criteria record the intent:
- `SDK-CES-INTENT-AC-001`: the returned permission map must contain zero missing and zero unsupported additional role-scoped permissions while preserving subject and action meaning.
- `SDK-CES-INTENT-AC-002`: the SDK must use the caller-supplied FMAA token as its bearer credential and make zero independent FMAA token-acquisition requests.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: These criteria do not prove that [[entities/ces]] responses contain sufficient role information, and unmapped meaning remains a compatibility gap for explicit review.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Portal and tile policy criteria
- Deny entry when an authenticated SC user has no entitlement for any registered application entity. [UI-ENTRY-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-entry-ac-001)
- Hide the tile and deny direct launch when the tile has zero configured EMS2 entities. [UI-EMPTY-ENTITY-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-empty-entity-ac-001)
- Show and authorize launch of a tile with one configured EMS2 entity and zero configured subjects when the user qualifies for portal entry and holds entitlement for that entity. [UI-EMPTY-SUBJECT-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-empty-subject-ac-001)
- Validate tile access on login, page reload, and session extension when idle. Which entitlement source and freshness apply to each event remains open. [UI-TILE-VALIDATION-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-tile-validation-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The historical draft principles require matching both the configured EMS2 entity and subject when a tile requires a subject. This remains draft design context. [Historical configured-subject rule](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#historical-configured-subject-rule)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The earlier owner answers name the [[entities/portal-team]] for the entry and two empty-configuration rules across local, test, UAT, and production. The November answer names the RATAN team for portal policy ownership and review under ICS bank security policy. Publication review and deployed enforcement remain pending. [Portal policy ownership](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-authentication-and-sessions.md#summary)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
## Entitlement lifecycle and risks
The SDK overview recommends entitlement caching and mentions NGINX stickiness for multiple endpoints. It also announces removal of EMS2 details from authentication JWTs in DEV on 30 August 2024, but that announcement does not establish the present DEV state or any production token shape.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Permission revocation takes effect in the UI on the next login. Behavior in an already-open tab before that login remains open. [UI-ENTITLEMENT-REVOCATION-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-entitlement-revocation-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: For protected API calls, revocation takes effect when the applicable Auth Server Redis entry expires. The entitlement cache has a one-hour expiry and the JWT parsing cache has a two-hour expiry. Cache interactions and the relevant entries for each API remain open. The two settings apply to cache entries; JWT lifetime and a combined revocation deadline remain unspecified. [API-ENTITLEMENT-REVOCATION-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#api-entitlement-revocation-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Logout has a separate target of immediately revoking all of the user's portal sessions while leaving identity-provider sessions outside that scope. The SDK guides describe validation and entitlement retrieval. Each application owns the enforcement of its protected operations. [PORTAL-LOGOUT-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-authentication-and-sessions.md#portal-logout-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:

- No downstream service execution or SDK compatibility build was inspected. The artifact and configuration for each consumer remain unresolved.
- Approval and deployed enforcement of the entry and tile rules remain unverified.
- How do the caches for each API interact, and when must revocation be visible in an already-open tab?
- Which CES data preserves each legacy role-specific grant for SDK 3.0.0 compatibility?
- Which failure-handling contract should SDK 3.0.0 callers use?
- What trusted control replaces JWT validation on excluded paths or configured skip headers?
- Where does each downstream service enforce subject and action permissions?
- Which current environments remove entitlements from authentication tokens?

preservation_map.claim:

Authentication and sessions, admin and onboarding, the registered SDK source copy `single-ui-auth-sdk`, the contracts `single-ui-sdk-jwt-validation`, `single-ui-sdk-request-context`, `single-ui-sdk-entitlement-lookup`, the authentication runtime baseline, and the active session renewal requirement provide related context. preservation_map.claim: This is a candidate requirement describing *intended target behavior* for portal session renewal. Human publication review is still pending, so the criteria express requested ideals rather than proof that the supplied implementation already conforms.

preservation_map.claim: ## Core intent
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
- Mouse, keyboard, and scroll activity must each support continued session renewal — see [[concepts/session-activity-renewal]].
- Idle timeout is at most 15 minutes. Absolute timeout is at most 60 minutes from portal authentication and applies during eligible activity and renewal.
- Within the absolute deadline, a usable refresh token can support recovery after idle expiry. Continued activity can support renewal across the initial refresh credential expiry while access remains valid.
- At the absolute deadline, the portal requires a new authenticated session.
- Manual recovery from an idle-expiry prompt must keep the prompt open until renewal succeeds, and must allow retry after a rejected request — see [[concepts/session-expiry-prompt-recovery]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Acceptance criteria (9 scenarios)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: [Canonical acceptance criteria](../../../records/candidates/requirements/REQ-active-session-renewal.md#acceptance-criteria).
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
| ID | Scenario | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Eligible mouse movement continues when renewal is due | ≥1 successful renewal before access expiry and the absolute deadline |
| AC-2 | Eligible keyboard input continues when renewal is due | ≥1 successful renewal before access expiry and the absolute deadline |
| AC-3 | Eligible scrolling continues when renewal is due | ≥1 successful renewal before access expiry and the absolute deadline |
| AC-4 | Eligible activity after initial refresh-credential expiry and before the absolute deadline, with valid access | ≥1 subsequent renewal in the current session |
| AC-5 | Manual renewal pending before the absolute deadline | 0 premature prompt closures |
| AC-6 | Requested renewal succeeds before the absolute deadline | Exactly 1 closure, after completion |
| AC-7 | Refresh-based renewal rejects | 0 closures; retry while the token remains usable and the absolute deadline has yet to pass |
| AC-8 | No eligible activity or manual renewal | Idle expiry within 15 minutes of last eligible activity |
| AC-9 | The session reaches its absolute deadline during eligible activity | 0 successful protected requests or renewals using that expired session |
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Key distinctions and boundaries
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
- AC-1 through AC-3 prescribe no fixed event cadence or renewal interval. Version 9 removes unsupported timing fixtures. The 15- and 60-minute ceilings come from the 12 November clarification. The prior four-hour criterion belongs to the earlier requirement.
- Portal-document activity is in scope; activity inside cross-origin embedded applications requires **separate integration evidence**.
- Expired or revoked credentials cannot authorize renewal; recovery with no usable credential and provider failures remain separate boundaries.
- Cancellation handling and request-sharing behavior have **no approved criterion here**; their disposition belongs in the gap record.
- Implementation, rollout, backlog, and conformance evidence belong in the independent intent-to-reality gap record, which cannot modify these criteria.
